legend: CD68 (PGM1) immunohistochemistry with Golgi/cytoplasmic dot staining of Langerhans cell histiocytosis cells.
The histopathology of both juvenile xanthogranuloma and Erdheim–Chester disease can show a cellular infiltrate of plump epithelioid cells with a variable number of Touton giant cells.
Monomorphic cellular infiltrate of small cells with finely vacuolated cytoplasm.
The CD163 stain highlights lesional histiocytes with surface staining in xanthogranuloma lesions of both juvenile xanthogranuloma and Erdheim–Chester disease.
The factor XIIIa stain highlights lesional histiocytes with cytoplasmic staining in both juvenile xanthogranuloma and Erdheim–Chester disease, with less staining in highly lipidized cells.
Staining for S100 highlights the large Rosai–Dorfman cells in the sinus of the lymph node with frequent emperipolesis.
The large Rosai–Dorfman histiocytes have abundant pale eosinophilic to watery-clear cytoplasm, often with emperipolesis and a large hypochromatic nucleus with distinct nucleolus (arrowheads).
